Docs-only change; no functional risk. Two substantive problems.

1. The stated rationale is inverted. proselint has no check that flags the right single quotation mark `’`; the relevant check is `typography.symbols.curly_quotes`, whose message is literally `Use curly quotes “”, not straight quotes "".` (verified in proselint `proselint/checks/typography/symbols.py`, pattern `\"[\w\s\d]+\"`). So converting `’` → `'` does not make these files proselint-compliant; it is a house-style choice, and it moves away from the direction this repo's own generators take — `docs/_scripts/generate_cli_docs.py:106` and `docs/usr/tools/generate.py:110` are `fix_curly_quotes()` helpers that rewrite straight quotes *to* curly ones in generated docs. Either restate the PR as "normalize apostrophes to ASCII" or drop it.

2. The change is not scoped. It also rewrites two URLs, one of which is dead: `https://wiki.ubuntu.com/Full_Disk_Encryption_Howto_2019` returns HTTP 404 today (wiki.ubuntu.com is now a fresh MediaWiki instance whose banner states "Legacy content may be unavailable and page links may have changed"). Details inline. Note CI will not catch this: `.github/workflows/ci.yaml:238-243` runs only `make lint-md` and `make html` for docs — no `linkcheck`, no `vale`.

Consistency: the conversion is partial across the doc set. 36 files under `docs/` still contain `’` (e.g. `docs/explanation/deploying-machines.md:19,27,33,42,52,80`, which this PR touches but leaves curly), and the touched files keep curly double quotes (`manage-machine-groups.md:424,428,437`, `what-maas-shouldn-t-do.md:46,50`). Because `smartquotes` is not in `myst_enable_extensions` (`docs/conf.py:322-327`), source punctuation is published verbatim — the site will now render mixed straight/curly apostrophes. If this normalization is wanted, do it in one scripted sweep over all of `docs/`; otherwise revert.

Mechanics are otherwise clean: no content, link-text, or anchor changes beyond the two URLs, and no apostrophes inside code fences or inline code were touched.

docs/explanation/security.md.110: Broken link introduced. I fetched `https://wiki.ubuntu.com/Full_Disk_Encryption_Howto_2019` — HTTP 404; the relaunched Ubuntu wiki does not carry this legacy page. The old `help.ubuntu.com/community/...` form is still the indexed, content-serving URL. Either revert this hunk or, better, point at a maintained page: `https://documentation.ubuntu.com/security/security-features/storage/encryption-full-disk` (verified live, covers LUKS/TPM FDE). Also unrelated to the proselint cleanup — split it out. `make linkcheck` (docs/Makefile) catches this class of error; CI does not run it.

docs/explanation/deploying-machines.md.40: `https://canonical.com/juju` verified live, so this is harmless — but it is a URL change in a PR described as apostrophe normalization. Move it (and the security.md one) to a separate `docs:` commit so the link churn is reviewable on its own.

docs/how-to-guides/manage-machine-groups.424: This file is now fully ASCII-apostrophe but retains curly double quotes here and at 428/437 — and line 430 uses straight double quotes (`"team A can only deploy machines in pool X."`), which is the character class proselint's `curly_quotes` check targets. The result is three quoting styles in one section. Pick one convention and apply it to the whole file.

docs/uncategorized/use-cases-server-life.7: `smartquotes` is not enabled in `myst_enable_extensions` (docs/conf.py:322), so this is a visible rendering change, not just a source change: this page will publish `'` while 36 other pages under docs/ still publish `’`. Worth a repo-wide sweep rather than per-file edits.

docs/uncategorized/what-maas-shouldn-t-d.3: Same partial-conversion issue: apostrophes are now ASCII but curly double quotes remain at lines 46 and 50, so the page mixes typographic and ASCII punctuation.
